source.title: InternImage: Exploring Large-Scale Vision Foundation Models with Deformable Convolutions
source.authors: Wenhai Wang; Ji-Feng Dai; Zhe Chen; Zhenhang Huang; Zhiqi Li; Xi-Zhou Zhu; Xiao-Wei Hu; Tong Lu; Lewei Lu; Hongsheng Li; Xiaogang Wang; Y. Qiao

record.tranche_reason: The study evaluates scaling and performance of vision models, but does not test language-model cross-entropy power laws, their extrapolation, or compute-optimal allocations. It cites Kaplan et al. in background discussion but does not use that result as a method or assumption.
record.gate_note: The paper reports vision classification accuracies across InternImage sizes and data fractions. These are related scaling results, but do not measure held-out language-model loss, fit or test a power law, or establish predictive extrapolation. Record them under fits_no_version; cited results from other work are not recorded as rows.
record.test_reason: A vision CNN architecture paper. It cites Kaplan et al. only in related work, as NLP-domain context. It reports ImageNet top-1 accuracy for models of different sizes and data regimes, but fits no power law, measures no held-out loss, tests no extrapolation and studies no compute-optimal allocation. Its accuracy numbers are a related but different construct and do not test any version as stated.
record.authors_conclusion: Essentially correct. The authors conclude that InternImage, a DCNv3-based CNN, scales to over 1B parameters and 400M images. They say it matches or beats large ViTs on classification, detection and segmentation, so CNNs remain a viable direction for large-scale vision foundation models. They note latency of DCN operators as a limitation.
record.recipe_differences: The study evaluates a vision CNN and does not reproduce the original language-model scaling-law method.
record.method_sensitivity: The paper reports different classification accuracies for InternImage-H at input scales 224² and 640²; it also varies ImageNet-1K data fraction in a separate experiment.

fits_no_version.finding: InternImage ImageNet top-1 accuracy rises with model size (83.5→88.9/89.6%, 30M→1.08B). Data, pretraining and resolution change alongside size, and no power law is fitted.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: Vision CNN classification accuracy increases with combined parameter and data scale-up. No functional form is established.

fits_no_version.finding: InternImage-T accuracy at 1%, 10% and 100% of ImageNet-1K data is 5.9%, 56.0% and 83.5%. The paper frames this as robustness to data scale, not as a scaling law.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: Accuracy of a vision CNN grows with training-data fraction. The three points are not fitted.

fits_no_version.finding: Table 8: at ~95–118M parameters, different depth/width scaling factors give ImageNet accuracy from 81.8% to 84.9%. This is a ~3-point spread in accuracy, not loss, for a vision CNN.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: For vision CNNs at similar parameter count, the depth/width split can change accuracy by several points. This is loosely analogous to V4, but uses accuracy, not LM loss.

record.problems: The study does not report held-out language-model loss, fit power laws, or test extrapolation. The relevant scaling results are vision accuracies under differing model sizes, data regimes, and—in the large model—input resolutions; no uncertainty estimates are reported for these results.
record.rows_left_out: No relevant reported scaling outcomes were omitted.

untested.parts: All: no held-out LM loss, and no power-law fit in N, D or C.
All: no extrapolation from small-run fits.
All for language-model loss. The depth/width comparison is vision accuracy only (see fits_no_version).
No power-law form is fitted for vision. Only raw accuracies at a few sizes and data fractions.
No relation of downstream performance to pretraining loss or to a fitted scale trend.
All: no fitted exponents to compare.

record.verdict_notes: The only mention of scaling laws is a related-work citation of Kaplan et al. as NLP context. The model 'scaling rules' are EfficientNet-style depth/width compound scaling chosen by accuracy, not loss power laws. No row bears on any version, and no verdicts are given.

versions.untested_parts: Held-out language-model loss as a function of parameters, tokens, or compute.
Prediction of larger-run loss from fits to smaller runs.
Compute-optimal parameter/token allocations and their growth with compute.
Loss changes from varying architecture at fixed parameter count across a wide range.
Power-law loss behavior in vision or other modalities and training regimes.
Predictability of downstream task performance from pretraining loss or scale.
Dependence of fitted loss exponents or compute-optimal splits on setup and fitting choices.
